explanation_steps: The textbook: 'History thus began five thousand to six thousand years ago, when people first began to write and keep records. The period before written records is called prehistory.'

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is <u>incorrect</u> about history?

options.A: It is periodically limited to the past.
options.B: Legends and myth constitute the main sources of history.
options.C: History helps us to understand how societies were governed.
options.D: The study of cause and effect is the central concept of history.
options.E: History helps us to establish a proper sense of identity.

explanation_steps: The textbook: 'history is different from legends and myths. History scientifically deals with events… in the past; whereas legends and myths are stories… which are most of the time scientifically unsupported narratives.'

Myths and legends 'help us understand the past' but they are not the main sources – historians rely on written, oral and material sources. The other statements agree with the textbook (history = study of the past; cause and effect is central; history gives identity and shows how societies were governed).
Answer: B.
tips: History = scientific, evidence-based; myths/legends = unsupported stories.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following best differentiates history from myths and legends?

options.A: History is always written in books
options.B: History is based on scientifically supported evidence
options.E: History does not deal with causes

explanation_steps: History deals scientifically with past events; myths and legends are mostly unsupported narratives.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct about Calendars?

options.A: The Babylonians were the first people to develop a calendar.
options.B: Gregorian is the most widely used calendar throughout the world.
options.C: Hejira calendar is mainly used by the Islamic communities.
options.D: Geez, Hejira and Gregorian calendars are widely used in Eritrea.

explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The Babylonians were probably the first people to develop a calendar' (A); 'The Gregorian calendar is the most widely used calendar throughout the world' (B); it lists 'the Islamic calendar or Hegira Calendar' (C).
In Eritrea the Gregorian (official/civil), Geez (Orthodox Church) and Hijra (Muslim community) calendars are all in use (D) – the textbook assignment asks students to describe them.
All four are correct. Answer: E.
tips: Babylonian = lunar 12×30; Egyptian = solar 365; Julius Caesar = Julian; Gregorian = today's world calendar.

similar_questions.stem: The Egyptian solar calendar had

options.A: 12 months of 30 days and 5 extra days

explanation_steps: Textbook: 365 days = 12 × 30 + 5 extra days.
Answer: A.

questions.review_flag: The textbook says the Babylonians were 'probably' the first to develop a calendar; the paper states it as fact. E is still the intended key.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is <u>incorrect</u> about the Caste System of India?

options.A: It was a set of rigid social divisions.
options.B: It determined a person’s occupation and economic potential.
options.C: Dravidians had equal status with the Aryans.
options.D: It was based, in part, on skin color.
options.E: It was introduced to India by the Aryans.

explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The clash between conquering Aryans and conquered Dravidians created a set of social and class divisions… The caste system of ancient India was a set of rigid social divisions that determined not only a person's occupation and economic potential but also his or her position in society, based partly on skin color.'
The conquered Dravidians were placed at the bottom, not equal to the Aryans. Answer: C.
tips: Caste order: Brahmins → Kshatriyas → Vaisyas → Sudras → Untouchables.

explanation_steps: Brahmins = priests, the highest caste.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true about the British Military Administration (BMA) in Eritrea?

options.A: It treated Eritreans and Italians equally.
options.B: The BMA was a period of economic prosperity in Eritrea.
options.C: The BMA officially allowed the formation of political parties in 1946.
options.D: The British favoured complete independence of Eritrea.
options.E: The BMA completely destroyed the Italian administrative systems.

explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Until October 1946, the British Military Administration prohibited the formation of political parties… But in October 1946, BMA officially allowed the formation of political parties.'
The BMA kept Italian officials and laws, favoured Italians, dismantled the economy after the war boom ended in 1945, and planned to partition Eritrea. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements refers to the gradual abrogation of the Federal arrangements by Ethiopia?

options.C: Replacement of the Ethiopian Penal Code by the Eritrean one
options.D: Abolition of the Eritrean Workers’ Union

questions.stem: Write any <u>two</u> reasons that led to the decline of the Byzantine Empire. (2 points)
questions.answer: Any two of: incompetent rulers after the Macedonian dynasty; power struggles between military leaders and aristocratic families, causing political and social disorder; the schism (split) between the Eastern Orthodox Church and the Roman Catholic Church; foreign invasions – above all the Seljuk Turks (defeat at Manzikert, 1071, loss of Asia Minor), the Crusaders' sack of Constantinople (1204) and finally the Ottoman conquest of 1453; continuous Islamic attacks.
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'the empire began to decline when incompetent successors came to power. Struggles for power between military leaders and aristocratic families led to political and social disorder… The Byzantine Empire was also weakened by a growing split between its church – the Eastern Orthodox Church – and the Catholic Church of the West… The greatest challenge came from the advance of the Seljuk Turks' (1071).
It 'survived until it was completely occupied by the Ottoman Empire in 1453'.
marking_points: 1 point each for any two: incompetent rulers; power struggles/disorder; church schism; Seljuk Turks (1071)/foreign invasions; Crusaders 1204; Ottoman conquest 1453.
tips: Internal (bad rulers, power struggles, church split) + external (Seljuks, Crusaders, Ottomans).
